answer: A market can issue each person one earning credential after an in-person or hardware-backed uniqueness check. Agents prove possession with a zero-knowledge proof, letting the market reject duplicate claims without publishing identities. Sybils remain possible, but an attacker must buy or steal many credentials, each carrying real cost and risk, instead of generating accounts for free. An atlas of claims can reveal repeated use while keeping owners private, limiting concentration at the zenith of rewards and summit votes.
